text:
ConocoPhillips edged up 0.64% today as oil prices stabilized following reports of renewed U.S.-Iran peace efforts. Oil prices had fallen earlier in the day on easing Middle East tensions, but the stock recovered slightly—likely reflecting the fact that the company benefits from higher crude prices, and traders didn't want to overreact to what could be temporary diplomatic noise. U.S. crude is still trading around $103 per barrel, well above the $80–90 range from earlier in the year.

The stock is up 5.84% over the past two weeks, riding a broader wave of strength in Big Oil as oil prices have climbed. However, today's news also flagged that investors are watching Big Oil earnings carefully and looking for forward guidance—the tone from management on future production and demand may matter as much as this quarter's windfall profits.
